what: What the libFuzzer runs of the fourteen targets found, read off the logs of two runs of the workflow `fuzz.yml`: the last one on a schedule and the last one on a pull request.
why: Until now the documents recorded one run of eight targets and one of ten on Windows (engine-round-2026-11, 07 and 14). The weekly run was recorded nowhere, and three targets added since (`truehd_multi`, `stream_push`, `eac3_program_config`) had no run recorded at all.
method: `gh run view <id> --log`, and from each target's job the lines libFuzzer prints at its end under `-print_final_stats=1`: `Done N runs in S second(s)`, `stat::number_of_executed_units`, `stat::new_units_added`. A log was also searched for `crash-`, `ERROR: libFuzzer` and `SUMMARY:`; none of the three occurs in either. The flags are those of the workflow: `-max_len=65536 -timeout=25 -rss_limit_mb=2048`, the seeds cut from the committed fixtures.

runs.note: the weekly run; at that commit the workflow had eleven targets
the last run of all fourteen targets; a pull request gives each ninety seconds

findings: Neither run found a crash, a timeout or an input over its memory limit.

`truehd_multi`, `stream_push` and `eac3_program_config` have run for ninety seconds each and never for the ten minutes of the weekly run: no scheduled run has started since they were added. The next one, on a Monday, is the first.
`eac3_program_config` is the slowest target, 24 executions a second, and `verdict_parity` the next at 57; ninety seconds give them 2,178 and 5,196 inputs.
open: The corpus a run builds is not kept: `fuzz/corpus/` is ignored and a runner starts from the seeds each time, so no run stands on the one before it.
No run of the weekly length exists for three of the fourteen targets.
